title: Premium, Policy Fee and Surplus Lines Tax Build-Up on Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)
content:
The term premium, policy fee and surplus lines taxes of an **Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)** policy are built up and booked under this rule.

## Retired clause

> The annual term premium is the excess dwelling limit divided by 1,000 times the tier's dwelling rate per 1,000 plus the excess personal property limit divided by 1,000 times the tier's personal property rate per 1,000, multiplied by the zone factor for the property's flood zone from the tier's zone factor table, reduced by the tier's elevation credit percentage when an accepted Elevation Certificate on file shows the lowest floor at least the tier's credit threshold in whole feet above the base flood elevation, plus the tier's loss-of-use charge, rounded to the cent once at the end and never less than the tier's minimum premium.

This clause is **no longer in force** as a clause of this rule. It is superseded by the current basis: a renewal term booked on renewal takes the renewal term premium figured on the renewal basis, and every other term premium is the excess dwelling limit divided by 1,000 times the tier's dwelling rate per 1,000 plus the excess personal property limit divided by 1,000 times the tier's personal property rate per 1,000, multiplied by the zone factor for the property's flood zone from the tier's zone factor table, reduced by the tier's elevation credit percentage when an accepted Elevation Certificate on file shows the lowest floor at least the tier's credit threshold in whole feet above the base flood elevation, plus the tier's loss-of-use charge, rounded to the cent once at the end and never less than the tier's minimum premium.

## Clauses in force

1. The tier's policy fee is added for each term.
2. The surplus lines tax and the stamping fee are the policy's recorded surplus lines tax rate and stamping fee rate of the taxable amount — the term premium plus the policy fee when the tier makes the policy fee taxable — each rounded to the cent.
3. Each term is booked as a term premium item, a policy fee item, a surplus lines tax item and a stamping fee item, and full payment being required means the whole amount is due at binding or renewal with no installment plan.
4. A payment is applied to the policy and term named on it, never moved to another policy, and a dishonored payment is reversed and handled under the insurer-cancellation rule.

The tier's dwelling and personal property rates and its minimum premium are the tier's own figures.

## Tax build-up, worked (hypothetical figures)

A term premium of 1000.00, a policy fee of 150.00 that is taxable, a recorded surplus lines tax rate of 5 percent and a recorded stamping fee rate of 0.2 percent: the taxable amount is 1150.00; the surplus lines tax is 57.50 and the stamping fee is 2.30, each rounded to the cent on its own. The term is booked as four items totalling 1209.80, all due at once.

superseded_clauses: The annual term premium is the excess dwelling limit divided by 1,000 times building_rate_per_1000 plus the excess personal property limit divided by 1,000 times contents_rate_per_1000, multiplied by the zone factor for the property's flood_zone from zone_factor_table, reduced by elevation_credit_pct when an accepted Elevation Certificate on file shows the lowest floor at least elevation_credit_threshold_ft whole feet above the base flood elevation, plus loss_of_use_premium, rounded to the cent once at the end and never less than minimum_premium.
